title_en: The Great Dhol (a long devotional song)
translation:
**Now begins Shri Vadu Dhol ||18||**

1. The Lord is incomparable, the one Supreme Self (Parmatma); Hari, Hari — you are the master of the soul, you are its very owner.
2. Vishnu, Govind, Narayan, Ram, Krishna — Hari, Hari — all of these are names of Parbrahm (the Supreme Reality).
3. O soul, look into your own self and break your bonds; Hari, Hari — thunder out the Name, do japa (repetition) of Parbrahm.
4. This alone is the highest good, this alone is knowledge; Hari, Hari — that meditation which is upon the name of Parbrahm.

|| Valan (refrain) ||

5. Great is the name of Parbrahm; it is the very home of righteous action.
6. Sages and siddhas rush to it in meditation; the lords of yoga gaze upon it through knowledge.
7. Vidhi (Brahma) and Shambhu (Shiva), the makers of creation — even they do not reach the far shore of his glory.

|| Valan ||

8. They do not reach the far shore of your glory, O Lord; his way cannot be found out.
9. Supreme Person, unthinkable, unmanifest — you alone are the self-existent Master.

**|| Aad ||1||**

1. Through the four wombs of birth I have wandered countless times; Hari, Hari — I never found the essence, O Lord, O Lord of liberation.
2. That light which is present in the very atom stands pervading everything; Hari, Hari — up to Hari, Har (Shiva), Brahma and all the rest.
3. Without remembering him one is never released; Hari, Hari — the soul lies bound, O Lord, in a tight, dense bond.
4. He has no form, no birth-caste, no kind or category; Hari, Hari — for him there is neither night nor day.

|| Valan ||

5. He for whom there is no day or night — worship that Light with the mantra.
6. He for whom there is no age or aeon — great beyond measure is his resolve.
7. He from whom you came into being, O soul — of him I make the refrain of my speech.

|| Valan ||

8. Of him I make the refrain of my speech: the capable and mighty Hari you have not served.
9. One who is not a devotee of the Father — know it for certain, that son has gone to ruin.

**|| Aad ||2||**

1. Sun and moon burn at his command; Hari, Hari — how shall I describe the forms he takes?
2. Earth and sky rest upon his support; Hari, Hari — how then can there be any limit to him?

|| Valan ||

3. How can there be any limit to him? Hari himself is the ten avatars.
4. Sun and moon abide by his command; how shall I tell of his forms?
5. Give up all poison, O fool — why have you forgotten the suffering of worldly existence?

|| Valan ||

6. Why have you forgotten the suffering of worldly existence? In distress, remember Govind alone.
7. He it is who establishes Brahma and Shankar; he it is who gives Indra his kingdom.

**|| Aad ||3||**

1. Crores of universes stand upon his word; Hari, Hari — how then can anything be his equal in weight?
2. His light pervades all that is unmoving and all that moves; Hari, Hari — keep your loving affection for the saints alone.

|| Valan ||

3. He sports with the saints with great affection; the all-pervading light is in every form.
4. He holds the universes by his word; there is no other who is his equal.
5. Hasten to his feet; abide in the practice of the duty of your station (varna-dharma).

|| Valan ||

6. Abide in the practice of the duty of your station; honour the one word of Vishnu.
7. Do not let sin and merit stain you in this way; you will be freed from the pain of worldly existence.

**|| Aad ||4||**

1. Shabda-Brahma (the Word as Brahman) is in love with Parbrahm; Hari, Hari — and I am intoxicated with your name.
2. Unmanifest Lord, endless, stainless; Hari, Hari — destroyer of the fear of rebirth, Shri Vasudev.

|| Valan ||

3. The devotee turns aside worldly existence and hell; that Parbrahm is the unmanifest one.
4. He who shapes the world and breaks it — no one grasps in what manner he is.
5. He in whom there is no division of any kind; whose word is the four Vedas.

|| Valan ||

6. He whose word is the four Vedas — do not abandon the original path.
7. Straying onto the wrong track of man-made doctrines — why do you fall into hell, ignorant fool?

**|| Aad ||5||**

1. He who has drunk the nectar of the unmanifest Consciousness; Hari, Hari — he has set his foot upon the head of Death.
2. Sacrifice, charity, austerity, pilgrimage, vows and mantras — Hari, Hari — all of these render their service in the name of Parbrahm.

|| Valan ||

3. All of them serve the Name; receive the fruit that it yields.
4. The fruit that is handed over is Parbrahm himself; so make yourself free of karma.
5. Let the mind run to that which is beyond the mind; thus the wall of the fear of rebirth is wiped away.

|| Valan ||

6. Thus the wall of the fear of rebirth is wiped away for one who serves with the mind's full conviction —
7. having slain the enemies: greed, delusion, lust, envy, anger and pride.

**|| Aad ||6||**

1. The unmanifest Consciousness that I had not attained; Hari, Hari — now I bind my thought upon your form.
2. Dhruv, Shuk and Narad — all of them he established; Hari, Hari — he gave them an unshakable place.

|| Valan ||

3. He gave an unshakable place to whoever repeated the Name alone.
4. Hari, Krishna, Keshav, Ram — thus many are his names.
5. He whose reign is unshakable — he has need of nothing.

|| Valan ||

6. He has need of nothing; yet the King fulfils what is in the devotee's mind.
7. To give the joy of the telling of his virtues, for that reason he takes birth in this manner.

**|| Aad ||7||**

1. The fear of karma lasted only so long; Hari, Hari — only as long as I was far away from you.
2. Prakriti (material nature) drove the soul into hell; Hari, Hari — it loaded it with crores upon crores of karma.

|| Valan ||

3. Consider the burden of a crore of deeds; they did not serve the mighty one.
4. He whose judgements are true; the shrutis and shastras have laid down their rulings.
5. Those who did not abide by that law — they were handed into the hands of Yam (death).

|| Valan ||

6. They were handed into the hands of Yam; for their deeds there are many dark hells.
7. Endlessly they suffer sorrows of every kind; the soul plays out that emptiness.

**|| Aad ||8||**

1. This ignorance has covered over the light of the eyes; Hari, Hari — blind, he forgot his home and fell into a well in the forest.
2. There the black serpent bit him; Hari, Hari — and he fell headlong into its mouth.

|| Valan ||

3. Again the dull-witted one fell into its mouth; the blind man does not see himself being destroyed.
4. O mind, let go of every other thought; take up that by which you may cross beyond worldly existence.
5. O mind, give up that scrap of pleasure; set your love upon Parbrahm.

|| Valan ||

6. Set your love upon Parbrahm day and night; O devotee, do not fail in your meditation.
7. You will attain unshakable happiness and rest; leave off the company of Prakriti.

**|| Aad ||9||**

1. Sunk in stupor by the poison of intoxication, he has lost his consciousness; Hari, Hari — how should such a one remember his home?
2. The true guru, the snake-charmer, pinned down the serpent; Hari, Hari — he awakened the blinded soul.

|| Valan ||

3. He awakened the blind one at that very moment — the one who had been in the blaze of delusion.
4. What greed there was for gathering wealth; many an agitation arose from it before.
5. Attachment to son, wife and kin; many times over there has been separation.

|| Valan ||

6. Many times over there has been separation; and still he holds the world in his mind.
7. In that which comes into being again and again and is wiped out again — what essence is there in it?

**|| Aad ||10||**

1. Sent by the Father, the snake-charmer came; Hari, Hari — with the medicine of knowledge he drew out the poison.
2. The collyrium-rod of the company of saints (satsang, holy company); Hari, Hari — that very instant the sight became clear.

|| Valan ||

3. In that instant the vision became pure; the saints' words are a rain of nectar.
4. The finest medicine is union with Parbrahm, by which the disease of worldly existence was driven out.
5. The teaching is meditation on Parbrahm; at daybreak the sun has risen.

|| Valan ||

6. At daybreak the incomparable sun has risen; the night spent in delusion is gone.
7. Letting go of [worldly] hope I found refuge; I have left the whole matter in you.

**|| Aad ||11||**

1. You are forever; I am not, not even once. Hari, Hari — this sense of "I" came to me only out of delusion.
2. Taking great pains he drew me out of the well; Hari, Hari — he showed me the road and sent me home.

|| Valan ||
